headline: Gold Drops Toward $4,000 as High Energy Prices Stoke Fed Inflation Concerns
summary: Gold slipped toward $4,000 an ounce as persistent energy prices renewed inflation worries ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision, even as buying demand from China helped cushion the metal's retreat.
why: Gold is a non-yielding safe-haven asset whose price typically moves inversely with real yields and interest-rate expectations set by the Federal Reserve.

impacts.name: Gold
impacts.why: Inflation fears linked to energy costs threaten to prolong elevated Federal Reserve policy rates.
